newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Firm on crude, regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Firm on crude, regional demand.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were firm at midday on Wednesday following sharp hikes to overnight crude values amid strong regional demand for prompt cargoes, traders said.
"The markets took off this morning because of the strong crude market," one broker said.
April gas oil swaps were last quoted at $26.20/$26.40 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $25.70/$25.80 per barrel, brokers said.
The market traded earlier in the day at $26.20, $26.27 and $26.30 per barrel, they said.
The April/May time spread widened and was last quoted at $0.80/$1.00 per barrel compared to Tuesday's traded level of 60 cents.
Traders said the widening spread reflected the strong demand for prompt cargoes from local traders where a premium of $1.60 per barrel was paid for cargoes loading a mere five days earlier.
One Tuesday five cargoes totalling 750,000-barrels traded at between $27.00-28.60 per barrel, free-on-board Singapore.
Overnight May Brent crude closed up a hefty 75 cents to $20.25 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
The strong crude numbers filtered through to the other product markets where April naphtha was quoted up 50 cents from Tuesday.
April naphtha was last quoted at $24.60/$24.95 per barrel in thin trading, brokers said.
Fuel oil also rose on the back of the crude market with April last quoted at $100.00/$101.50 per tonne, up from Tuesday's $99.50/$100.50, they said.
